entry.summary:
Safe, secure, sovereign AI for Māori GIS projects

AI is showing up everywhere. Some of it is useful, some of it is risky, and much of it isn’t explained in ways that make sense for iwi and hapū GIS contexts.

In this video, GIS Specialist Duane Wilkins shares practical tools and techniques that can be applied across a range of Māori GIS mapping kaupapa. Whether you're new to AI or already experimenting, this kōrero focuses on real-world use rather than theory, helping you apply AI in ways that make sense for your mahi.

Learn how to use AI in ways that protect your data, strengthen your mapping capability, and uphold the integrity of your work on the whenua.

You’ll gain a clear, jargon-free understanding of what AI tools actually do, along with practical ways to safely trial AI on your own computer without exposing sensitive information. The session also explores how AI can speed up mapping, reporting, and data preparation while highlighting key risks around privacy, ownership, and external platforms.

This video is especially relevant for iwi and hapū working with whenua and data, Māori trusts and organisations managing land and assets, GIS practitioners wanting practical and accessible approaches to AI, and anyone responsible for data who wants to better understand the risks before using these tools.

Using AI without understanding it can put your data at risk, while ignoring it entirely means missing out on tools that can save time and support better decision-making.

You’ll leave with a clearer understanding of how AI can support your kaupapa — and where to draw the line to protect your data, your people, and your work.
